classification.difficultyReason: Sketch vertically translated reciprocal graphs, identifying asymptotes and calculating exact intercepts.

content.prompt: Sketch each graph, showing the asymptotes and any intercepts.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=\frac{2}{x}$ one unit up. The asymptotes are $x=0$ and $y=1$.

At the $x$-intercept, $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=\frac{2}{x}+1\\\frac{2}{x}&=-1\\x&=-2.\end{align*}$$
The $x$-intercept is $(-2,0)$. There is no $y$-intercept because the expression is undefined at $x=0$. The graph passes through $(1,3)$.

spec.description: Complete reciprocal graph with both branches, coordinate axes, horizontal asymptote and labelled intercept and reference point. The y-axis is the vertical asymptote.
spec.mathematics: y=2/x+1; asymptotes x=0 and y=1; x-intercept (-2,0); point (1,3); no y-intercept.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=\frac{4}{x}$ three units down. The asymptotes are $x=0$ and $y=-3$.

At the $x$-intercept, $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=\frac{4}{x}-3\\\frac{4}{x}&=3\\x&=\frac{4}{3}.\end{align*}$$
The $x$-intercept is $(\frac{4}{3},0)$. There is no $y$-intercept because the expression is undefined at $x=0$. The graph passes through $(-1,-7)$.

At the $x$-intercept, $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-\frac{12}{x}+4\\\frac{12}{x}&=4\\x&=3.\end{align*}$$
The $x$-intercept is $(3,0)$. There is no $y$-intercept because the expression is undefined at $x=0$.

At the $x$-intercept, $y=0$:
